newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban hold opposition-claimed town-witness.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban hold opposition-claimed town-witness.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia on Friday were in control of the strategic northeastern town of Pul-i-Khumri, which its opponents said they had taken, witnesses said.

Ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani's ambassador to India, Masood Khalili, said earlier on Friday in New Delhi that Pul-i-Khumri, in Baghlan province, which the Taleban captured on Wednesday, had been retaken by opposition forces overnight.
But the town, on the main highway from the capital Kabul to the north, was firmly in Taleban control on Friday and was calm, witnesses said.
They said there was a large attendance at mosques in Pul-i-Khumri for traditional Friday congregations.

Khalili told a news conference in New Delhi that opposition forces also controlled the strategic Salang Pass, about 100 km (60 miles) north of Kabul, they had taken Pul-i-Khumri overnight and were advancing towards Charikar, a main town south of the pass.
There was no immediate independent word about the status of the Salang Pass, which a Taleban convoy crossed earlier this week.

However, a Pakistan-based private Afghan news service reported that opposition forces of renowned guerrilla commander Ahmad Shah Masood had taken the towns of Golbahar and Jabal-os-Seraj south of the Salang Pass and were fighting further south aiming to take Charikar, capital of Parwan province.
The Taleban government was set up after the militia, led by Islamic theology students, captured Kabul last September. The Taleban now control nearly 90 percent of the war-shattered country.
